PASSO 1: sem artigo ou sem sinal de gêne: STEP 1: English adjectives never change: "the big man", "a big woman", "big children". German adjectives before a noun ALWAYS take an ending. STEP 2: the ending depends on the word in front: if the article already shows gender and case clearly (der, die, das), the adjective relaxes into a weak -e or -en; if there's no article, or the article doesn't show enough (ein), the adjective takes over that job with a strong ending. STEP 3: after «sein» the adjective takes NO ending: «Der Tisch ist groß».
O português põe o adjetivo depois do sub: English puts the adjective before the noun too — so word order is easy for you. The challenge is the ending: English "new" stays "new"; German says «der neue Tisch», «den neuen Tisch», «ein neuer Tisch», «neues Brot».
O adjetivo antes do substantivo, passo a: The adjective before a noun, step by step
PASSO 1: depois de «sein», o adjetivo NÃ: STEP 1: after «sein», the adjective does NOT change: «Der Mann ist groß» (the man is tall). STEP 2: BEFORE the noun, it takes an ENDING: «der große Mann» (the tall man). STEP 3: after the definite article (der, die, das), there are only two endings: «-e» and «-en». STEP 4: in the NOMINATIVE singular, it's always «-e»: der große Mann, die kleine Frau, das neue Auto. In the plural, «-en»: die großen Kinder. STEP 5: in the ACCUSATIVE, only the MASCULINE changes: «den großen Mann» (-en); feminine and neuter stay «-e»: «die kleine Frau», «das neue Auto»; the plural stays «-en». STEP 6: the ending repeats the case the article has already shown — after der/die/das, the adjective just "rests" on -e or -en, because the article does the heavy lifting.
o português muda o adjetivo por gênero e: English adjectives never change at all ("the tall man", "the tall women"). German adjectives change by gender, number AND case — but after der/die/das there are only two endings to choose from: -e and -en.

PASSO 1: no DATIVO, depois de der, die,: STEP 1: in the DATIVE, after der, die, das, the ending is «-en» for ALL genders and the plural: «dem großen Mann», «der kleinen Frau», «dem neuen Auto», «den großen Kindern». STEP 2: in the GENITIVE, the ending is also «-en»: «des großen Mannes», «der kleinen Frau», «des neuen Autos», «der großen Kinder». STEP 3: sum it up like this: there is «-e» in only five places (nominative singular in all three genders, plus accusative feminine and neuter); everything else is «-en». STEP 4: use them after dative and two-way prepositions: «mit dem neuen Auto» (with the new car), «in der kleinen Küche» (in the small kitchen).
